the_blocking_fact.headline: Nothing on this site can earn money today, and the fix is one string the owner has to supply.
the_blocking_fact.detail: Amazon requires Associates tags to be embedded in the product links on the site declared in the application, and it reviews an application only once at least three qualifying sales have been driven within the first 180 days. This site has zero tagged links, so it has zero qualifying purchases, so the application cannot be reviewed. Meanwhile the three links the whole project was built around are themselves short links carrying no tag, so even the supplied links would not attribute a sale to the owner. Every downstream capability in the brief — conversion tracking, the optimizer, the revenue model, the API enrolment that would let the site publish prices and ratings — sits behind this one missing value.

what_is_settled: The three supplied links resolve, on four separate dates across four sessions, to the same three listings: a Chefman 6-quart dual basket, an Emeril Lagasse 26-quart French-door oven, and a Chefman 8-quart basket fryer (BR-19, BR-20, BR-21).
The evidence discipline holds at scale: {{pages_disclosed}} pages carry the disclosure, no page prints a product price, and every specification row links to the page it was read from.
The machinery is trustworthy: {{gate_count}} of {{gate_count}} workflow steps pass locally, and the counts that matter are derived from the tree rather than typed.
The rules are known and quoted: what may be published, what may not, and where the disclosure has to sit.
what_is_not_settled: Whether the three listings are the products the brief meant. Nothing in any official document binds a supplied code to a product (BQ-18).
Whether an Associates account exists at all, and if it does, its tag and marketplace (BQ-14, BQ-19).
Which of the 18 published surfaces is the site that would be declared (BQ-15).
Who writes it, under what name, and whether that name is public (BQ-16).
What readers are searching for. There is no demand signal anywhere in the project, so no topic on the topics board can be ranked by expected volume (BQ-20).

decide_first.why: Declaring one site determines what every other change is a change to. It is also the only decision that has to be right before an application names a URL, because an application is not reassessed after a rejection.
Supplying the Associates tag is the owner's one action that unblocks the entire revenue side. It takes one sign-in and no code.
It costs under an hour and it is reversible. The T55 rebuild removed the phrase from every reader-facing page; 14 operator and companion pages still carry it.

the_one_thing: If only one thing happens next, it should be the tag. Everything the brief asks the platform to do with real traffic — track it, convert it, optimize against it — is unreachable until a link on a page can be attributed to the owner.
